label: Pay-per-order AI phone answering: flat fee vs percentage
h1: Pay-per-order AI phone answering: flat fee vs percentage of the order
seoTitle: Pay-per-order AI phone answering for restaurants
description: AI phone answering that charges per order: how a flat $0.90 fee compares with 2%, 6% and 10% of the order and $1.50 per order, at $15 to $80 tickets.
lead: Several AI phone services for restaurants now charge only when an order comes in. They price it in different ways, and the difference grows with your ticket size.
question: What is the cheapest AI phone answering for restaurants that charges per order instead of a monthly fee?
answer: Per-order AI phone services usually charge either a flat fee per order (commonly about $0.90 to $3) or a percentage of the order (commonly about 2% to 10%). ROAL charges a flat $0.90 per completed order with no monthly fee. A 2% fee is cheaper on tickets under $45; on a $50 order a flat $0.90 beats 2% ($1.00), 6% ($3.00) and 10% ($5.00).

pains.title: Percentages grow with your ticket
pains.body: A percentage fee takes more from your biggest orders: the family dinner, the office lunch, the catering tray.

pains.title: Extra fees hide in the fine print
pains.body: Some per-order plans add card processing, setup, or a minimum. Compare the all-in cost per order, not just the headline rate.

pains.title: Monthly plans charge on slow weeks
pains.body: A fixed monthly fee is due whether your phone brought in 5 orders or 500.

verdict: If your average phone order is above about $45, a flat $0.90 is the lowest per-order price in this comparison, and the gap grows with bigger tickets. If most orders are small, a low percentage can cost a little less, so run your own numbers with your average ticket and monthly phone orders.

sections.h2: Work out your real cost per month
sections.body:
Take two numbers from last month: how many orders came in by phone, and your average phone ticket. Then compare:

1. **Flat fee:** orders × fee. 300 orders × $0.90 = **$270**.
2. **Percentage:** orders × average ticket × rate. 300 × $35 × 2% = **$210**; at 6% = **$630**; at 10% = **$1,050**.
3. **Higher flat fee:** 300 × $1.50 = **$450**.

Swap in your own numbers. The [AI phone host cost calculator](/tools/phone-host-cost-calculator) does this for you, and the [missed call calculator](/tools/missed-call-calculator) shows what the unanswered calls are worth first.

sections.h2: What to check besides the rate
sections.body:
- **What counts as an order.** ROAL only bills a confirmed order whose ticket reached your kitchen screen. Ask others how they treat cancelled or voided orders.
- **Card processing.** Some services take payment on the phone and add processing fees. ROAL doesn't take cards on the phone; guests pay at pickup the way they already do.
- **Minimums and setup.** Look for monthly minimums, onboarding fees or contracts.
- **Where the order goes.** A kitchen screen, your POS, a text or a fax. Make sure your kitchen will actually see it during the rush.
- **Who handles the hard calls.** Allergies, complaints and catering should reach a person. See [when phone AI should hand off to staff](/blog/when-ai-should-hand-off-to-staff).

Per-order pricing keeps quiet weeks cheap and only grows when the phone is making you money. A fixed monthly plan, often in the range of roughly $79 to $599 per location, can make sense only when your phone order volume is high and steady. For most independent restaurants, per-order is the lower-risk way to start. More on that in [pay per order vs monthly AI phone plans](/compare/monthly-ai-phone-plans) and on [ROAL pricing](/pricing). Running a pizza shop? See the same math at pizza ticket sizes in [AI phone answering for a pizza shop with no monthly fee](/compare/pizza-shop-no-monthly-fee).

faq.q: Is there an AI phone answering service for restaurants with no monthly fee?
faq.a: Yes. Several now charge per order instead. ROAL charges a flat $0.90 per completed order with no monthly fee, setup fee or contract, and calls that don't become orders are free.

faq.q: Is a percentage fee or a flat fee cheaper for phone orders?
faq.a: It depends on your ticket size. A 2% fee costs less than $0.90 on orders under $45 and more above that. Higher percentages like 6% or 10% cost more than $0.90 on almost any order over $15.

faq.q: What does ROAL count as a completed order?
faq.a: A confirmed order (items, name and phone) whose ticket reached your kitchen screen. Hang-ups, wrong numbers, questions and test calls are not billed.

faq.q: Does ROAL take card payments on the phone?
faq.a: No. It never asks for card numbers, so there are no phone processing fees from ROAL. Guests pay at pickup or however you already take payment.

faq.q: How do I try ROAL before paying?
faq.a: Paste your restaurant's website or Google Maps link at tryroal.com/try. ROAL builds a phone host from your menu in about two minutes and you can call it from your browser with no sign-up.
